BREAKING: The US economy has now experienced 78 consecutive months of expansion, the 6th-longest business cycle since 1854.

This is well above the long-term average of ~49 months and the median of ~38 months.

By comparison, the longest period without a recession was between 2009 and 2020, at 128 months.

All 5 of the most recent US expansions rank among the 7 longest economic growth periods since business cycle dating began in 1854.

Unconventional monetary policy, historically large budget deficits, alongside the AI investment boom, appear to be extending the duration of business cycles.

The data says the US economy is remarkably strong.

I think if any asset can have credit built on it, then that attempt will be made and it will come down to its properties. It’s not really a choice.

Bitcoin has a faster withdrawal and audit cycle than gold. That matters.

Either that is enough or it is not. I’m not opposed to digital credit per se.

Luke made money on bitcoin. He made early-cycle OG gains (paid off his mortgage in a prior cycle I think, now trading it.) Lately he has been on the bearish side which was right for a while and wrong recently.

Honestly, the last macro guy I’d go after as a bitcoiner is Luke.

At that point it seems more “eating your own” than anything. Or “don’t look a gift horse in the mouth”.

Luke is a fan of global, portal money, and neutral reserve assets, and ways to mitigate fiscal dominance on investors. He is ripe for bitcoiners but is rightly skeptical or trading on certain areas and can benefit from high quality information given to him on the discussion scale or macro scale.

He is not the droids you’re looking for.

Those are a ton of words but here are a few things.

-I've been critical on treasury companies in general, only invested in two public ones and avoided the rest. Strategy, which I've been long since August 2020, has outperformed bitcoin over a 6+ year period. Two out of three times I've been an analyst on Strategy earnings calls, I've been the *bear* questioner. I asked them about how they're managing risk at the top of the autumn 2025 market. I asked them how they're managing leverage on Stretch back in Feb 2026 before the blow-up, which they recovered from.

-Orange Juice raised money privately. We could have gone public during the hype of 2025 (we were actively in the market from spring 2025) but we chose *not* to, since we never found an aligned deal and were concerned with what we were seeing.

-Orange Juice investors of course have risks. They're private, accredited investors at this time. But they have a liquidation preference that means that they get 1.5x before any founders including me could cash out.

-Other than our main operating partner, five of the six Orange Juice founders, including me, take zero salary. The liquidation preference means I don't get a dime until we pass the 1.5x threshold. I might work for 2-3 years and get zero compensation for this, if I'm wrong. It's all about shareholder protection. I only benefit if initial shareholders get a return on their money.

I appreciate your general concerns, but I'd invite you to do more research before posting sensationalist types of posts.
